mainTopic: Doubts about חמץ moved by animals: the נפל in the pit, hiding leftover חמץ (אביי, רבא, רב מרי), and mouse cases compared to קבוע, רוב, and שאני אומר.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: a woman threw a נפל into a pit, a כהן looked in, and the חכמים ruled him טהור because weasels and martens (חולדה וברדלס) live there. The גמרא asks whether this means a ספק overrides a ודאי, and it gives two answers. Either it is ספק against ספק, because maybe it was not a real נפל, or it is ודאי against ודאי, because such animals certainly drag food away. Next, the גמרא asks why the next משנה says to hide leftover חמץ if we do not worry about a חולדה. אביי splits the 13th from the 14th of ניסן. רבא rejects this ('is the marten a prophet?') and says we hide it only so a חולדה won't take it in front of us, and a ברייתא supports him. רב מרי gives another reason: one might put down ten pieces and find nine. Finally, the גמרא matches cases of mice taking מצה or חמץ to known rules: קבוע (the nine stores), פירש (follow the majority), and שאני אומר (the two baskets). It begins to push back on the last comparison, and that pushback continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the story: the כהן looks in and the חכמים rule him pure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its story. A כהן looked into the pit to check whether the נפל was male or female, and the חכמים ruled him טהור because weasels and martens are common there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a כהן came and peered into the pit to find out whether the baby was male or female. The case came before the חכמים, and they declared him pure, because weasels and martens are found there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about a stillborn baby thrown into a pit. The ruling is that the כהן who looked in stays טהור. This story is the setup for the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being over a dead body would normally make a כהן טמא through טומאת אהל. The חכמים said he is pure anyway, because animals that drag food into their holes live there. So the body was probably no longer in the pit when he looked in.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest. He must avoid becoming impure from a dead body.
He peered or leaned over to look.
A weasel and a marten. These animals drag food away to their holes.

steps.confusionAlert: Why did the כהן care whether the baby was male or female? It matters for how long the mother is impure (ויקרא פרק יב). It has nothing to do with the כהן's own impurity. That detail becomes important in step 4.

phrases.english: And a priest came and peered at it
phrases.notes: Leaning over the pit could put him under the same 'roof' as the corpse (טומאת אהל).

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם זָכָר הוּא אִם נְקֵבָה הִיא.
phrases.english: to know whether it was male or whether it was female.
phrases.notes: This tells the mother how many days she is impure.

phrases.english: And the incident came before the Sages, and they declared him pure,
because a weasel and a marten are commonly found there.
phrases.notes: These animals likely dragged the body away before he looked.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (source text being used against אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי)
steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָא כֹּהֵן וְהֵצִיץ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן is טהור, because weasels and martens in that area probably dragged the נפל away.

steps.title: Challenge: here a doubt seems to override a certainty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the נפל was certainly thrown in, and it is only a doubt whether animals dragged it away. Yet the חכמים ruled leniently, so it looks like a ספק is overriding a ודאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, it is certain that she threw it in, and it is only a doubt whether they dragged it away at that time or not. And yet a doubt comes and pulls us away from a certainty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי using this ברייתא. In the ברייתא, a doubt seems to win over a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The certainty is that a dead body was put into the pit. The doubt is whether animals removed it before the כהן looked. Ruling him טהור lets the doubt beat the certainty, which contradicts the rule the גמרא has been using.

keyTerms.meaning: A certainty; something we know for sure.
A doubt; something that may or may not be so.
She threw it in or cast it in.
Takes us out of a certainty, meaning it overrides it.

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי is what the whole sugya depends on for the חמץ-and-mouse case. If this ברייתא breaks the rule, that whole line of reasoning falls.

phrases.english: But here, where she certainly threw it in,

phrases.aramaic: וְסָפֵק גֵּרְרוּהוּ וְסָפֵק לֹא גֵּרְרוּהוּ הָהִיא שַׁעְתָּא,
phrases.english: and it is uncertain whether they dragged it or did not drag it at that time,
and yet a doubt comes and overrides a certainty!
phrases.notes: This is the punch of the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּוַדַּאי הֵטִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling in step 1 to attack the principle אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A certain corpse is in the pit and its removal is only a doubt, yet the ruling is lenient. So a ספק overrode a ודאי.

steps.title: Answer one: maybe it only looked like a נפל
steps.stepSummary: Read the ברייתא as saying she dropped something that looked like a נפל. Then there are two doubts, and the rule is not broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say 'she threw a stillborn into a pit.' Say instead 'she dropped something like a stillborn into a pit.' Then it is a doubt against a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the ברייתא. Maybe it was never certain that a real נפל was in the pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the object might just have been a lump of blood or tissue, which does not make anyone impure, there is no certainty of a corpse at all. So we have a doubt (was it a נפל?) and another doubt (was it dragged away?). A ספק against a ספק can be ruled leniently without breaking the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say this, rather say that. A formula for rereading a text.
A doubt against a doubt; there is no certainty on either side.

phrases.english: Do not say 'that she threw a stillborn into a pit,'
rather say: 'that she miscarried something like a stillborn into a pit,'
and so it is a doubt and a doubt.
phrases.notes: There is no ודאי for a ספק to override.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא שֶׁהֵטִילָה נֵפֶל לְבוֹר אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A real נפל was certainly in the pit, so the lenient ruling lets a ספק beat a ודאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is unknown whether it was a real נפל, so it is ספק against ספק and the rule stands.

steps.title: Challenge: the ברייתא only doubts whether it was male or female
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא says the כהן looked to know if it was male or female. That suggests it was certainly a baby, and the only question was its gender.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches 'to know whether it was male or female'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks answer one using the ברייתא's own words. If the only question was the baby's gender, it was clearly a real נפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking 'male or female?' only makes sense once we know it is a formed baby. So the reading 'something like a נפל' seems to contradict the ברייתא's wording. That would bring back the problem of a ספק against a ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches; the ברייתא explicitly says.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא ״לֵידַע אִם זָכָר הוּא אִם נְקֵבָה הִיא״ קָתָנֵי!
phrases.english: But it teaches 'to know whether it was male or whether it was female'!
phrases.notes: This implies the baby's existence was certain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לֵידַע אִם זָכָר הוּא אִם נְקֵבָה הִיא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's only stated doubt is about gender, so it must have been a real נפל. That makes it ודאי again.

steps.title: Answer: the כהן had two questions, one after the other
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means the כהן first wanted to know whether it was just a shapeless mass or a real נפל, and then, if it was a נפל, whether it was male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: to know whether she miscarried 'wind' (a shapeless mass) or a real stillborn. And if you conclude it was a stillborn, then to know whether it was male or female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends answer one by explaining that the ברייתא's words hide two layers of questions. The gender question was only the second question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question was whether there was a real baby at all. Only if there was did the gender matter. So the ברייתא does not prove the נפל was certain, and the 'ספק וספק' answer still works.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; the גמרא is explaining what the text really intends.
Literally 'wind'. Here it means a shapeless miscarriage that is not a real baby.
And if you conclude, meaning if it turns out that.

steps.whatToRemember: Answer one: the case is ספק וספק. It was unclear whether a real נפל was there at all, and the gender question only applied if it was.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם רוּחַ הִפִּילָה, אִם נֵפֶל הִפִּילָה.
phrases.english: to know whether she miscarried 'wind' or whether she miscarried a stillborn.
phrases.notes: The first question: was there a real baby at all?

phrases.english: And if you conclude that she miscarried a stillborn:

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם זָכָר הוּא וְאִם נְקֵבָה הִיא.
phrases.english: to know whether it was male or whether it was female.
phrases.notes: The second question only applies if the answer to the first is yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵידַע אִם רוּחַ הִפִּילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 and keeps answer one in place.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gender question shows it was certainly a נפל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gender question was only a follow-up. The main doubt was whether it was a נפל at all.

steps.title: Answer two: the dragging is itself a certainty
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the case is a certainty against a certainty. Where weasels and martens are common, they certainly drag the body away right away. They may leave some leftovers, but they certainly drag it off.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you prefer, say: there it is certainty against certainty. Since weasels and martens are found there, they certainly dragged it away at that time. Even though they leave leftovers, they at least certainly dragged them away at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the challenge of step 2. The animals' dragging is treated as a sure thing, not a doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where these animals are common, we are sure they take food right away. So the certain corpse is met by an equally certain removal, which is ודאי against ודאי. Someone might object that the animals leave scraps behind. The גמרא answers that leaving scraps does not matter, because they still drag the food off to their holes, not leaving it in the pit.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say. This introduces an alternative answer.

steps.confusionAlert: Answer two does not say the animals certainly ate the body. They may leave scraps. It only says they certainly dragged it out of the pit, and that is enough to make the כהן טהור.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
there it is a certainty and a certainty,
since a weasel and a marten are commonly found there,
they certainly dragged it away at that time.
Granted that they leave leftovers,
phrases.notes: This anticipates an objection.

phrases.aramaic: מִיגְרָר מִיהַת וַדַּאי גֵּרְרוּם בְּהָהִיא שַׁעְתָּא.
phrases.english: still, as for dragging, they certainly dragged them at that time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא הָתָם וַדַּאי וּוַדַּאי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recategorization: the removal is ודאי, not ספק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Whether the animals removed the body is only a doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where these animals are common, removal is certain, so it is ודאי against ודאי and the rule אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי is untouched.

steps.title: Another version: not certainly eaten, but certainly dragged to their holes
steps.stepSummary: A second version of answer two says: we don't claim the animals certainly ate the body, but we do claim they certainly dragged it to their holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: even though we don't say they certainly ate them, we do say they certainly dragged it to their holes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records a slightly different wording of answer two. The core idea, a certain dragging away, stays the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version separates eating, which is not certain, from dragging to their holes, which is certain. Both versions agree the body certainly left the pit. That is all that matters for the כהן's purity. So the case stays ודאי against ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same statement.

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers protect the rule אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי. (1) ספק וספק: maybe there was no real נפל. (2) ודאי וודאי: animals certainly drag food away, even if they don't certainly eat it.

phrases.english: (Another version:
granted that we do not say they certainly ate them,
that they certainly dragged it to their holes, we do say.)

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא נְהִי דְּוַדַּאי אֲכָלוּם לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate wording of the answer in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the case depends on whether the animals ate the body.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating is not certain, but dragging to their holes is, and that is enough.

steps.title: Contradiction from the next משנה about hiding leftover bread
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says we don't worry that a חולדה dragged חמץ. But the סיפא (next משנה) says to hide leftover חמץ so it won't need another בדיקה, which suggests we do worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really say we don't worry that a marten dragged the bread? But the next משנה teaches: whatever bread you leave over, put it in a hidden place, so that you won't need to search again after it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule in our משנה that we don't worry about a חולדה dragging חמץ. It quotes the next משנה, which seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the next משנה tell us to hide leftover bread, unless we fear a חולדה might take it somewhere? That fear sounds exactly like the worry our משנה said to ignore. So the two משניות seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: A weasel or marten, a small animal that drags food away
The later clause, here the next משנה
In a hidden or protected place
Leaves over (bread kept after the search)

phrases.english: And do we really say we are not concerned
that perhaps a marten dragged it?
But isn't it taught in the latter clause:
What he leaves over, he should put in a hidden place,
phrases.notes: The bread kept for eating after the search

phrases.english: so that it will not require searching after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא גֵּרְרָה חוּלְדָּה? וְהָא קָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the נפל discussion back to the basic rule of the משנה about the חולדה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that we don't worry a חולדה dragged חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The next משנה requires hiding leftover bread to avoid another search, which implies a worry about the חולדה.

steps.title: אביי: the 13th is different from the 14th
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the rulings refer to different days. When bread is everywhere (the 13th), a חולדה eats and doesn't hide it. When bread is scarce (the 14th), she stores it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It's not a problem. This ruling is about the fourteenth, and that ruling is about the thirteenth. On the thirteenth, when bread is found in every house, the marten doesn't hide bread. On the fourteenth, when bread is not found in the houses, it does hide it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by assigning each משנה to a different day. On a day with plenty of bread the חולדה doesn't hide it, and on a day with no bread she does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה (no worry) is about a time when bread is still common, so the animal just eats and doesn't stash anything. The next משנה (hide it) is about the 14th, when bread is gone from homes. Then a חולדה might hoard the bread and hide it, so we protect the leftovers.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult
this is on the fourteenth,
that is on the thirteenth.
On the thirteenth, when bread is common
in all the houses, it does not hide it.
On the fourteenth, when bread is not common
in all the houses, it hides it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא — בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, הָא — בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time (different days)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות speak about the same situation, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: No worry when bread is plentiful (13th); worry about hoarding when bread is scarce (14th).

steps.title: רבא: Is the marten a prophet?
steps.stepSummary: רבא mocks אביי's answer. A חולדה has no way of knowing that today is the 14th and that nobody will bake until evening, so it can't decide to save bread for later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is the marten a prophetess? Does it know that today is the fourteenth, and that people won't bake until the evening, so it leaves some over and hides it?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects אביי's distinction with a sharp rhetorical question. An animal can't plan around the calendar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer assumed the חולדה acts differently on the 14th because she 'knows' bread will be scarce. רבא points out that an animal can't know the date, or know that nobody will bake until that evening. So the time-based split does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: A prophetess, one who knows the future

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's question is not a real question about animal prophecy. It is a rhetorical way of saying אביי's answer is impossible.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: וְכִי חוּלְדָּה נְבִיאָה הִיא!
phrases.english: Rava said: Is the marten a prophetess?!
that it knows that today is the fourteenth,
and that people won't bake until the evening,
and so it leaves some over and hides it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי חוּלְדָּה נְבִיאָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer from step 9.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes an animal knows the date and plans ahead for a bread shortage.

steps.title: רבא's answer: only if we see the marten take it
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the next משנה differently. We hide the leftover bread because a חולדה might grab it right in front of us. Then we would know for sure that חמץ was moved, and we'd have to search again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Whatever bread you leave over, put it in a hidden place, in case a marten takes it in front of us, and then it will require a search after it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own resolution of the contradiction. The next משנה is not about a hidden worry, but about a case where we actually see the חולדה take the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says we don't worry about something we didn't see. But if we watch a חולדה carry off bread, we know for sure that חמץ is now somewhere in the house, and a new בדיקה is required. Hiding the leftovers prevents that situation, so the two משניות no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of us, as we watch

steps.whatToRemember: An unseen possibility (maybe a חולדה dragged it) is not a concern. A seen event (a חולדה took it in front of us) does require a new בדיקה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
What he leaves over, he should put in a hidden place,
lest a marten take it in front of us,
and it will require a search after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רָבָא: מַה שֶּׁמְּשַׁיֵּיר — יַנִּיחֶנּוּ בְּצִנְעָה, שֶׁמָּא תִּטּוֹל חוּלְדָּה בְּפָנֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי, רבא offers a new answer to the contradiction from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the reason behind the next משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hiding the bread shows we worry about unseen dragging by a חולדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hiding the bread is only to avoid a case where we see the חולדה take it, which would require a new search.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing as רבא: hide leftover חמץ so a חולדה won't come and take it in front of us and force a new search.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבא: Someone who wants to eat חמץ after the search, what should he do? Whatever he leaves over, he should put in a hidden place, so that a marten won't come and take it in front of us, and he will need to search after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the exact phrase 'in front of us' (בפנינו). That shows the concern is about seeing the חולדה take the bread, just as רבא said, and not about a time-based hoarding habit as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with him

steps.whatToRemember: A ברייתא supports רבא: leftover חמץ is hidden to avoid seeing a חולדה take it, which would require a new בדיקה. In the next step, רב מרי gives a different reason.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Rava:
One who wishes to eat leavened bread after the search,
what should he do?
What he leaves over, he should put in a hidden place,
so that a marten will not come and take it in front of us,
and he will need to search after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer from step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's explanation that the concern is only a חולדה taking bread in front of us
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explicitly says 'שלא תבוא חולדה ותיטול בפנינו'

steps.title: רב מרי: Hide it so you don't put down ten and find nine
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי gives his own reason why the next משנה says to hide leftover חמץ. A person might set aside ten pieces, find only nine, and then need to search again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: It is a גזירה, in case he puts down ten pieces and finds only nine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי offers a different answer to the contradiction from Step 8. He explains why the next משנה says to hide leftover חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the worry was a חולדה grabbing bread right in front of us. רב מרי's worry is about counting: the person knows he set aside ten pieces, and if he later finds nine, he knows one is missing and must search again. Hiding the חמץ well prevents this. Neither worry contradicts our משנה, which says we don't assume a חולדה dragged חמץ when we saw nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rule made by the חכמים to prevent a problem
He will put down / set aside

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
It is a decree, lest he put down ten
phrases.notes: He set aside ten pieces of חמץ found during the search.

phrases.english: and find nine.
phrases.notes: A piece is now clearly missing, so he would have to search again.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרִי אָמַר: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַנִּיחַ עֶשֶׂר וְיִמְצָא תֵּשַׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the סיפא, as an alternative to רבא's explanation in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the סיפא, so that it doesn't conflict with the רישא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hiding the leftover חמץ seemed to show that we worry about a חולדה dragging bread unseen.
steps.terutzMaskana: We hide it only because of a missing-count problem (ten became nine), which would be a known loss. It is not a general worry about unseen dragging.

steps.title: A mouse takes from nine piles of מצה and one of חמץ
steps.stepSummary: If a mouse took a piece directly from one of the piles and we don't know which, the case matches the 'nine stores' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are nine piles of מצה and one pile of חמץ. A mouse came and took a piece, and we don't know whether it took מצה or חמץ. This is the case of the nine stores.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic connected to animals taking food. It compares a mouse taking from the piles to a known case about nine stores.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mouse took directly from a pile, which stays fixed in its place (קבוע). A doubt about something קבוע is treated as 50/50, even though most of the piles are מצה. So the piece might be חמץ, and the house needs another search.

keyTerms.meaning: Something fixed in its place; a doubt about it is treated as 50/50

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the majority wins here just because nine piles are מצה. When the piece was taken straight from a fixed pile, the majority does NOT decide. It is treated as a 50/50 doubt.

phrases.english: Nine piles of matza
and one pile of chametz,
and a mouse came and took (from a pile).
phrases.notes: The mouse took directly from the piles.

phrases.english: And we don't know if it took matza
or if it took chametz
this is the case of 'nine stores.'
phrases.notes: In that case the doubt is forbidden, because of קבוע.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּשַׁע צִיבּוּרִין שֶׁל מַצָּה וְאֶחָד שֶׁל חָמֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from hiding leftover חמץ to a new set of cases where a mouse takes food of uncertain status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mouse taking directly from fixed piles creates a 50/50 doubt, like the nine stores, so the doubt is treated strictly.

steps.title: A piece came loose first, then the mouse took it
steps.stepSummary: If the piece had already separated from the piles before the mouse took it, the case matches the סיפא of the nine-stores teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a piece separated from the piles, and then a mouse came and took it, this is the case of the סיפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second version of the mouse case. Now the piece was already loose when the mouse took it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a piece has left its pile, it is no longer קבוע. A loose piece is assumed to come from the majority (כל דפריש מרובא פריש). Since most piles are מצה, we assume the piece was מצה, and no new search is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It separated / came loose from its place
The latter clause of a teaching
Anything that separated is assumed to come from the majority

phrases.english: If it separated,
phrases.notes: A piece came loose from one of the piles, and we don't know which pile.

phrases.english: and a mouse came and took it
this is the latter clause.
phrases.notes: This refers to the סיפא of the nine-stores teaching, quoted in Step 17.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֵּירֵשׁ, וַאֲתָא עַכְבָּר וּשְׁקַל — הַיְינוּ סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 14: a loose piece versus a piece taken straight from a fixed pile.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A piece that separated before the mouse took it follows the majority, so it is assumed to be מצה.

steps.title: The source: nine kosher stores and one non-kosher store
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the teaching: if someone bought from one of ten stores and doesn't know which, the doubtful meat is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: There are nine stores, all selling meat from properly slaughtered animals, and one store selling נבלה meat. If someone took meat from one of them and doesn't know which one, the doubtful meat is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source it referred to in Step 14, so we can see the rule for the 'nine stores' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer took the meat straight from a store, and a store stays in its place, so it is קבוע. That makes the doubt 50/50 even though most stores are kosher, and the meat is forbidden. This is the rule Step 14 applied to a mouse taking directly from the piles.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat from a properly slaughtered (kosher) animal
Meat from an animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: As we learned: nine stores,
all of which sell meat of slaughtered animals,
and one sells neveilah meat,
and he took from one of them,
and he does not know from which of them he took
his doubt is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Taken from a fixed place, so it counts as a 50/50 doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: תֵּשַׁע חֲנוּיוֹת, כּוּלָּן מוֹכְרִין בְּשַׂר שְׁחוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the comparison made in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a mouse taking directly from the piles creates a forbidden 50/50 doubt
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of the nine stores (introduced with דתנן)

steps.title: Meat found outside follows the majority
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of the teaching says that meat found outside follows the majority. This is the rule for the loose piece the mouse took.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with meat that is found, follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the teaching with its סיפא. This is the part Step 15 pointed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat found lying outside has already left the store, so it is not קבוע. We assume it came from the majority, which here means a kosher store. In the same way, a piece that came loose from the piles is assumed to be מצה.
steps.whatToRemember: Taken directly from a fixed place (קבוע) means a 50/50 doubt, which is treated strictly (nine stores / mouse takes from a pile). Separated first (פירש) means we follow the majority (meat found outside / loose piece of מצה).
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between קבוע and פירש is a basic tool used all over ש"ס for deciding doubts about mixtures.

phrases.english: And in a found case,
phrases.notes: Meat found outside, away from the stores.

phrases.english: follow the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַנִּמְצָא — הַלֵּךְ אַחַר הָרוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted teaching and gives the source for Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That a piece which separated before the mouse took it follows the majority
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the nine-stores teaching: וּבַנִּמְצָא הַלֵּךְ אַחַר הָרוֹב

steps.title: Two mice carry מצה and חמץ into two houses
steps.stepSummary: Two piles (מצה and חמץ) stand before two houses (searched and unsearched). Two mice each take one, and we don't know which entered which house. The גמרא says this is like the case of 'two baskets'.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two piles, one of מצה and one of חמץ. In front of them are two houses, one searched and one not searched. Two mice came. One took מצה and one took חמץ. We don't know which mouse went into which house. This is the case of 'two baskets'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new mouse case and matches it to a known case called 'two baskets'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the mouse with the חמץ went into the house that was already searched, which would mean it needs another search. The גמרא links this to 'two baskets', a case where we assume things landed in the matching place. If the comparison holds, we would assume the חמץ went into the unsearched house.

keyTerms.meaning: Two baskets (a known case about תרומה and חולין)

steps.confusionAlert: Both mice really did go into houses. The doubt is only about which mouse went into which house, not about whether a mouse brought anything in.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי צִיבּוּרִין, אֶחָד שֶׁל מַצָּה וְאֶחָד שֶׁל חָמֵץ.
phrases.english: Two piles, one of matza and one of leaven.
And in front of them, two houses,
one searched and one not searched.
And two mice came,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שְׁקַל מַצָּה, וְאֶחָד שְׁקַל חָמֵץ.
phrases.english: one took matza, and one took leaven.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדְעִינַן הֵי לְהַאי עָיֵיל וְהֵי לְהַאי עָיֵיל,
phrases.english: And we don't know which entered this one and which entered that one,
phrases.notes: The doubt is which mouse went into the searched house.

phrases.english: This is the case of two baskets.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ שְׁתֵּי קוּפּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of mouse cases (Steps 14-17), each matched to an earlier teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two mice, two houses, unknown which went where: this matches the 'two baskets' case.

steps.title: The two baskets teaching: we assume each fell into its own kind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the teaching. Two baskets (חולין and תרומה) fell into two סאה containers (חולין and תרומה), and the mixtures are permitted, because 'I say' each fell into its matching kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: There are two baskets, one of חולין and one of תרומה. In front of them are two containers of a סאה each, one of חולין and one of תרומה. These fell into those, and they are permitted. For I say: the חולין fell into the חולין, and the תרומה fell into the תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the 'two baskets' teaching to show the rule it just compared to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרומה might have fallen into the plain חולין, which would forbid that mixture to a non-כהן. The teaching still permits it, using the reasoning of שאני אומר: we assume the outcome where nothing became forbidden. Applied to our case, we would assume the חמץ mouse went into the unsearched house.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy produce given to a כהן, forbidden to others
Containers of a סאה (a measure) each
'For I say': we assume the version of events that keeps things permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: שאני אומר is a well-known leniency in cases of doubt. The next step tests whether it can be used for חמץ.

phrases.english: As we learned: two baskets,
phrases.notes: This teaching comes from the תוספתא.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: one of non-sacred produce and one of teruma.
And in front of them, two se'a containers,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאֶחָד שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: one of non-sacred produce and one of teruma.
And these fell into those: they are permitted.
For I say,
the non-sacred fell into the non-sacred,
and the teruma fell into the teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: שְׁתֵּי קוּפּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source text for the comparison made in Step 18.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The 'two baskets' teaching, which uses שאני אומר to permit the mixtures

steps.title: Pushback: when do we really say 'I say'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to question the comparison: 'Granted, we say שאני אומר...' The full limitation comes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that we use the reasoning 'for I say'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a rejection of the comparison. It grants that שאני אומר exists, and the next line will limit where it applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אימור signals 'fine, granted in that case, but...'. The גמרא is about to argue that the leniency in the baskets case may not carry over to our case of חמץ. The reason it gives comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say' or 'granted': opens a concession before a limitation

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not finished. Don't read it as agreeing with the comparison. It is the opening of a pushback that continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Say that we state "for I say"
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמְרִינַן שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting the comparison of Step 18 to the source quoted in Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the two-mice case and the two-baskets case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Opening concession only. The specific difference between the cases is stated on the next amud.
